sourceRules.occurrenceScope: All first-occurrence statements are within catalog 61-80 only, not library-first claims. Clock class 4 already occurs in accepted Doors 4.
sourceRules.movingDotMaskException: Property-mask misses retain movement; Contraction has 14 moving dots including two property-mask misses.
sourceRules.newControls: No new key or physical-controller binding established. Buster launch is a source contact path, not a newly invented shoot action.

GN.record: Grid position, placement word, color word, four-direction bit mask; version >7 adds 32-bit mode mask, otherwise 15. Filtering precedes capacity 18.
GN.appearance: Group 3200: 8 descriptors and 8 images. Color bases 0..2, barrel frames 3..6, destroyed frame 7. Shared background template; no persistent individual gun callback sprite.
GN.placement: Raw source origin offset (-22,-23) in Point word order, then 24 times placement quotient/remainder by 2. Exact x/y anchors remain to be native-qualified.
GN.activation: Enabled gun scans four source direction entries in order (mask bits 1,2,4,8), launches PR type 0 for set bits, then requests sound 35 even if shared projectile pool is full. By-color call scans allocated gun order. Cardinal projectile velocity is three source pixels per callback.
GN.bomb: GNBombed uses placement-dependent one/two-cell footprint, disables matched gun and paints destroyed frame 7; it does not scan or clear active projectiles.

TR.record: Grid position, placement, color, version >10 32-bit mask (otherwise 15); filter before capacity 18.
TR.appearance: Group 3300: 6 frames/images, idle frame 2*color and pressed frame 2*color+1, animation step 0; logical layer 9.
TR.activation: Each newly entering ordinary actor fires matching guns immediately, before occupancy increment. A second entrant fires even while occupied. Occupancy 0-to-1 selects pressed art; exit decrements and zero restores idle art. Holding occupancy alone does not repeatedly fire.
TR.ordering: WA finds first visible outline collision, compares cached trigger identity, activates new trigger before releasing old. Ordinary flag excludes rotating spikes and type-5 busters.
TR.bombAndReset: TRBombed hides footprint-matched trigger sprites. Reset restores visibility, placement, idle frame and occupancy 0; gun reset re-enables records. Active PR cleanup is separate.

PR.allocation: GN bullets and thrown busters share 32 reusable slots. First null slot wins; exhaustion returns without a clone or queue, while caller sound/hide/deadline side effects continue. Clone callback uses logical layer 9.
PR.bullet: Group 4200: 3 descriptors/images, color selects frame. Shared bullet template uses WA clock class 0 and step 0.
PR.callback: Advance source sprite animation, translate velocity once, reject raw base outside inclusive universe bounds, then first wall outline collision, then door collision. Outside/wall/ordinary-bullet-door hits mark sprite deferred-disposed and immediately clear pool slot.
PR.wall: PR type 0 requests sound 31 and is disposed. Type 1 requests sound 33, calls WLShatter and is disposed.
PR.door: Type 0 requests sound 32 and is disposed. Type 1 requests sound 34, reflects the velocity component selected by source door orientation and remains alive; no penetration rollback is present in this callback.
PR.human: PRCheckCollisions scans slot order, skipping null, invisible and type-1 projectiles, then checks original outlines. WACheckBullets invokes human death reason 16 before wall/door checks; it does not consult dot protection or consume the bullet. Ordinary enemy collision branch does not perform this bullet check.
PR.boundsAndReset: PRSetUnivBounds stores supplied universe bounds; demo mode expands them by 50. Normal play must use the caller-provided source bounds. PRReset removes/frees all active slots, clears them, retains template.
PR.orderingGate: Dynamic insertion and cached-next sprite traversal must follow the existing SU source contract. A bulk post-frame projectile update is not equivalent. Exact same-sweep insertion and simultaneous trigger/projectile/human cases need coordinator tests.

type5Buster.appearance: Group 3900: 64 angular descriptors, 41 images; source raw outlines and mirror/anchor metadata retained privately.
type5Buster.actor: Nonhuman layer 1, independent serialized clock class, nonordinary flag. This batch includes class 1 and 3 busters. Some have normal Pascal programs; do not freeze all busters at their initial pivot.
type5Buster.contactLaunch: WAHitEnemy takes the type-5 branch before ordinary protection handling. It derives a velocity vector from human canonical angle and angular sign using source SANE trigonometry/rounding, requests sound 41, temporarily zeros buster sprite step, clones it through PRActivate type 1, restores original step, hides original and stores resurrection deadline. This is not a generic player fire button.
type5Buster.velocityLimit: Source launch uses a six-pixel magnitude before integer rounding. Exact bit-for-bit SANE rounding and all-angle velocity vectors remain an integration gate; no replacement trigonometric helper is supplied.
type5Buster.clone: Type-1 clone preserves current angular art, zero angular step and original buster clock rather than bullet class-0 clock; it shatters walls, reflects from doors and is excluded from PR human-bullet collision.
type5Buster.resurrection: Difficulty deadlines add 300/600/900/1200 latched guest ticks. WAEnemyOneFrame auto-resurrects only saved spec type 5 when invisible, deadline nonzero and current tick strictly greater than deadline. WAResurrect sets visible true without rebuilding spec. Bomb-hidden ordinary types 1-4 do not auto-resurrect. Orphan expiry clears deadline and suppresses this return.
type5Buster.reset: Round reconstruction/reset must restore source actor state and remove separate PR clones; simply unhiding originals leaves projectile state behind.

programRebinding.semantics: Signed negative or index >= loaded WP count clears actor program pointer and sets PC 1; valid references scan Pascal records to the requested index. Mishmash has four active out-of-range references (5,6,7,11), one stored WP record and no resolved active programs. Do not modulo-wrap or fabricate programs. Generated boards should reject these references rather than silently authoring them.

movingDotUnknownBytes.semantics: Only e/n/s/w assign nonzero velocity. p and every other byte, including Slipstream l/r, take stationary default. PC still advances/wraps, and each instruction lasts 16 callbacks. Do not translate l/r into left/right.
movingDotUnknownBytes.mask: Movement survives property-mask miss. Stable dot identity, previous-position grab fallback, two-callback maximum delta wrapper and rider update remain required.

generationRequirements: Preserve serialized 8x11 indexing, separate display dimensions, source record order, actor identity, present pivots, mode masks and color bits. All twenty displays here are 11x8.
Filter WA/SP/PU/GO/WY/EL/HY/GN/TR by actual mask before allocation. BO/EX/WL/DR/DS are not filtered this way. Preserve inline movement on dot-property mask misses.
Keep actor class, angle, direction, Pascal PC and referenced program independently of type. Respect ordinary-only hooks; programmed and class-3 busters are present.
Validate GN color 0..2, placement variants and legal direction mask; match triggers by color and preserve first-overlap/entry/occupancy order. Do not introduce hold-to-autofire.

Preserve PR first-free allocation, capacity 32 shared by bullets and busters, immediate slot clear plus deferred sprite deletion, source list insertion and cached-next traversal. Pool exhaustion must still allow caller side effects.
Use original outline/anchor data and inclusive universe bounds; qualify wall shatter, door reflection and projectile/human collision order without visual-silhouette collision substitution.

Validate 18 guns, 18 triggers, 22 HY endpoints, 61 EX, 12 EL, 43 misc, 60 BO, 15 GO, 5 LI starters, 17 sparks, 6 explosions and 32 DP lifetime allocations against their distinct source allocation rules. Validate dynamic pool demand separately from static counts.

Require exactly two active HY endpoints per generated channel, valid high-channel frames and bounded nonempty inline Pascal programs. Chatter reaches HY22 and uses channel 23. Existing templates containing l/r must preserve stationary semantics; new generated programs should use explicit p.
Keep buster contact ordering, deterministic source-rounded velocity, clone clock and strict resurrection deadline; prevent ordinary enemies from acquiring buster resurrection behavior.

Preserve source RNG consumption in existing bombs, oil, goodies and death effects. No new RNG call was found in the traced GN/TR/PR/basic buster-launch paths, but this is not an exhaustive whole-round RNG proof.
Out-of-range goodie request 169 in Saga and Firing Line follows the source setter behavior; never reduce it modulo frame count.

Reject out-of-range program references in new generated boards. Imported Mishmash must reproduce source program rebinding: four references beyond its sole stored WP record become null program pointers with PC 1.
Generated boards require semantic and asset validation, solvability evidence and sequential native/runtime acceptance. This survey supplies requirements, not a generator or accepted board.

visualInventory.sourceColliderRule: Original RAW descriptor offsets and signed outline index retained. Scanline inclusive spans checked against descriptor dimensions; rectangles/absent outlines remain distinct.
visualInventory.existingVariants: Dot colors, ring/protection, up/down channels, doors/switches, spikes, puddles, goodies, connectors and HY variants remain in per-level JSON. This is inventory, not anchor or art acceptance.

validation.outOfRangeSourceBehavior: CODE6:f11c-f162 clears program pointer and resets PC to 1 when reference <0 or >= loaded program count.
validation.checks: Source assertions, source hashes, private descriptor/outline validation and focused disassembly review only.

uncertainties: No catalog 61-80 level is accepted, played, rendered or activated by this survey.
GN/TR/PR art anchors and high-channel HY appearance need native comparison; no asset conversion or candidate was made.
Exact SANE buster vector rounding, all-angle contact outcomes and source same-sweep insertion cases require bounded integration/native tests.
Deadline values are guest ticks; no new real-time speed measurement or timer-to-seconds conversion is claimed.
Static capacity checks do not prove dynamic pool demand or malformed-input safety.
Cross-mechanic interactions among moving/up-down dots, rings, HY/EX, doors, oil and bombs remain gated.
Source lookup/list order, universe-boundary equality and reset need focused runtime tests before any acceptance.
